note: Every `!important` the importance walk proved necessary, keyed by the rule's own text and the property, each with what it beats in the state that decided it (D9). The walk fails when a declaration it needs is not recorded here or a recorded one is no longer needed; `DSH_IMPORTANCE_LEDGER=write node packages/testing/e2e.cjs --scenario importance` writes it from a run, so the difference is read in the diff. The walk drops that one declaration's importance, reads the value the page falls back to over every longhand the property stands for, and takes each other candidate for it away in turn — the element's inline style, and every rule of every readable stylesheet that matches and declares any of those names, including another declaration of the same names inside the rule under test (a longhand written beside a shorthand); the ones whose removal moves the value, or starts a transition, are recorded. `inline` and `host-important` are what the weight is really needed for. An empty `opponents` means the walk could not attribute the fall-back to a candidate it scanned, not that nothing holds it: the declaration is load-bearing either way — the walk proved the value moves without its importance — and the open question is which declaration outside the scan takes over. Three hypotheses have been tried and do not account for today's thirteen: a transition starting (counted now), a longhand beside the shorthand in the same rule (a candidate now), and every matching element rather than the first (all of them now).
